jobs.title: Head of Growth & Partnerships, Law Schools
jobs.description: About Juno Juno leverages collective bargaining power to secure better student loan rates for graduate students. With 290,000+ members and over $2B in negotiated loan volume, we've proven that group buying works. We are the most popular way to pay for the world’s top graduate programs and are seeking a leader to help us grow even further among law students. The Problem: Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options, exactly what Juno provides.  ￼ Your mission:   We're seeking a leader to own our full-funnel growth for law schools. Your efforts will ensure every future lawyer gets fair, transparent financing options.  You'll build the playbook for reaching 200+ law schools and establishing Juno as the go-to resource for law student financing.  What you’ll do: Own the law school vertical: Build and execute GTM strategy, hit growth targets, and drive Juno member growth Scale distribution through partnerships: Negotiate national deals with key organizations that can help reach our target market Activate campus-based chapters with turnkey playbooks Build relationships with financial aid offices at target schools Partner with LSAT prep companies and law school admissions ecosystem Run targeted campaigns aligned to application cycles Build a campus ambassador network: Recruit, train, and manage high-performing law students across JD/LLM programs with clear KPIs and incentives Talk to members directly: Talk to students directly throughout the cycle. Calls, email, DMs, campus visits. You should know the top five reasons a law student with a rate offer never submits an application because you've heard them first-hand, not because a dashboard told you. Be the expert students trust: Become fluent in how graduate borrowing actually works — federal vs. private, what drives a rate, cosigners, in-school deferral, refinancing, and what changed under the new caps — and be the person who can give a 1L a straight answer. Drive cross-functional initiatives: Partner with product on feature development, collaborate with the CX/client happiness team, and ensure compliance on messaging Manage operations and analytics: Forecast pipeline, track cohort performance, optimize CAC/LTV, and manage budget allocation Partner with senior leadership to own waitlist growth → loan origination : landing pages, A/B tests, content, webinars, email/SMS, and event cycles aligned to application, admissions, and financial aid timelines What We Offer Compensation : Competitive base salary + performance bonus with significant upside potential. Compensation: $140k–$250k, including performance upside tied to growth milestones.  Benefits : Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and retirement matching  What We’re Looking For Background : Typically 3–5+ years or an outlier track record (e.g., you scaled a campus network, ran national org programming, built a zero‑to‑one motion). Preference for experience in professional services, management consulting, investment banking, or high-growth startups Preference for an Owner‑operator who has owned a number in growth/BD/marketplaces/fintech/edtech or campus‑scale programs. Ownership of a number, end to end: you'll carry the Law vertical's funded-loan target and the conversion rates underneath it. You're comfortable being both the person who explains a miss and the person who fixes it. Bias to action : ship experiments frequently; instrument attribution; close loops with lender relations & compliance. Fluency with your own data: you can find where students stall between a rate offer and a submitted application, and make the case for a fix with evidence rather than instinct. Relationship-building that compounds: schools, student organizations, ambassadors, admissions communities, and lender partners. Equally comfortable on a call with a target B2B partner and in a group chat with 1Ls. Comfort with seasonality : our year has a peak. You plan for it months ahead and go all-in when it lands. Tenacity : we work as hard as it takes to achieve our targets. The X-Factor You're hungry: Ready to own outcomes, not just make recommendations You're scrappy: Will do whatever it takes to win You're magnetic: Can recruit and inspire great people You think in systems: you'd rather build the process once than do the thing by hand ten times Interview process Intro chat → Hiring manager deep‑dive → Case (market entry + distribution plan) → Cross‑functional interviews (product, data, marketing, lender relations) → Founder conversation → References. Why Join Juno? The Opportunity Real Impact: Help hundreds of thousands of students get access to the lowest rates on the market  Market Timing: Federal aid changes create massive tailwind for growth  Proven Model: $2B+ negotiated, 290K+ members - product-market fit achieved

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
jobs.description: About Juno Juno leverages collective bargaining power to secure better student loan rates for students. With 290,000+ members and over $2B in negotiated loan volume, we've proven that group buying works. We are the most popular way to pay for the world's top graduate programs, and we're looking for someone to own the communications that reach our members at the moments that decide whether they borrow with us. The Problem: Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options, exactly what Juno provides.  ￼ Your mission:   We're seeking a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own the execution of our member communications across all our products and business lines. Juno sends at high volume to a member base of 290,000+, and the gap between a good send and a great one is measured in funded loans. You'll be the person who turns what we know about our members into the right message, to the right segment, at the right moment in their borrowing cycle, and who can prove what it did.  What you’ll do: Own lifecycle execution end to end: Build and ship email and SMS campaigns across grad, undergrad, and refi. Learn the Juno product and data model deeply: This is the core of the job: Understand how a member moves from signup to rate offer to application to funded loan Know what we hold on every member, where it lives, and what it can and can't tell you Use that structure to build segmentation and personalization that hold up at scale Build segments that are actually right: Define who receives what by vertical, school, application stage, loan status, and timing. A mis-scoped audience is the most expensive mistake in this role. Work in coordination with the people who own products/business lines: Translate the goals of grad leaders and senior team members into a shipped campaign calendar.  Own measurement: Report on what each campaign did. Opens and clicks, but mostly applications started, applications completed, and loans funded. Bring the read to the team before anyone asks for it. Run the test roadmap: Propose and run experiments on subject lines, timing, sequencing, and offers, and keep a record so we stop re-learning the same lessons. Keep the program clean and compliant: Route messaging through compliance review, maintain suppression and deliverability hygiene, and keep the account organized enough that someone else could pick up your work. Use AI as a multiplier: Draft, QA, and debug with AI tools. Segment logic, Liquid, SQL, copy variants, post-send analysis. We expect the work to move faster because of them, and we expect you to catch it when the output is wrong. What We Offer Compensation : Base salary range: $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience, plus an annual performance bonus. Benefits include comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage and 401(k) matching. Benefits : Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and retirement matching  What We’re Looking For Background : Typically 1–3+ years in lifecycle/CRM marketing, marketing operations, growth, or an analytical role adjacent to one of them. Open to a lifecycle marketer who wants to go deeper on data, or an analyst/ops person who wants to move into growth Hands-on experience with an ESP (Customer.io, MailChimp, Klaviyo, HubSpot) is a plus; we'll teach you ours Comfortable with data: You can read a funnel, reason about a segment, and tell a real result from noise. You don't need SQL on day one, but you should want to learn it. AI fluency: You already use AI in your daily work and can walk us through exactly how. We care less about which tools you use than whether you've actually changed the way you work, and whether you know where they fall down. Precision: The work is high-volume and unforgiving of small errors, because a wrong merge field or a mis-scoped audience reaches thousands of people at once. You check your work, and you build processes so the checking isn't the only thing standing between us and a mistake. Execution over ideation: You'll ship a lot. You'd rather run the calendar well than spend the week debating it. Curiosity about the product: You want to understand how student lending actually works, federal versus private, what drives a rate, cosigners, deferral, refinancing, because you can't segment well on a product you don't understand. Comfort with seasonality: our year has a peak. You plan for it months ahead and go all-in when it lands. Tenacity: we work as hard as it takes to achieve our targets. The X-Factor You're precise: You catch the broken link before it goes to 40,000 people You're curious about the data: When something works, your first instinct is to ask why You close the loop: A campaign isn't done until you've reported what it did You think in systems: You'd rather build the process once than do the thing by hand ten times Why Join Juno? The Opportunity Real Impact: Help hundreds of thousands of students get access to the lowest rates on the market.  Market Timing: Federal aid changes create massive tailwind for growth.  Proven Model: $2B+ negotiated, 290K+ members - product-market fit achieved.

jobs.title: VP of Finance
jobs.location: Remote or Hybrid in Miami, FL
jobs.description: About Juno Juno is the leading student loan marketplace. By organizing borrowers into collective bargaining groups, we negotiate better rates and terms than individuals could ever secure on their own — and we've saved members hundreds of millions of dollars in the process. We're a lean, high-caliber team that moves fast, ships often, and cares deeply about doing right by the people we serve. The Role We're looking for a VP of Finance to own our financial function end to end. This is a hands-on leadership role reporting directly to the founders. You'll be equal parts strategic partner and operator — building the models and infrastructure that guide the business while also rolling up your sleeves to close the books, run analyses, and answer hard questions with data. This is a startup, not a corporation. You'll build the finance function rather than inherit one, wear multiple hats, and thrive on ambiguity. If you want a large team and mature processes on day one, this isn't the role. If you want ownership, proximity to decisions, and real impact, read on. What You'll Do Own financial strategy and planning — build and maintain the financial model, drive budgeting and forecasting, and give the founders a clear line of sight into unit economics, and growth. Run the finance operation — accounting, month-end close, cash management, AP/AR, payroll, and audit readiness. You set up the systems and, early on, often run them yourself. Be the numbers partner to the founders — turn ambiguous questions into rigorous analysis, pressure-test decisions, and help set priorities. Lead fundraising and investor relations — support capital raises, manage the data room, and own board and investor reporting. Own compliance, tax, and risk — keep us clean and audit-ready as a company operating in the financial services space. Build for scale — stand up the tools, controls, and (eventually) the team that let finance keep pace with the business. What We're Looking For Proven experience as a finance leader (VP Finance, or senior finance operator), ideally with startup or high-growth company experience. Genuinely hands-on — comfortable owning both the strategy and the spreadsheet. No task is beneath you. Strong command of modern finance and business tooling — you're fluent in today's SaaS finance stack (e.g., ERP/accounting, FP&A, billing, BI) and comfortable working closely with a technical team and their systems. AI-forward — you actively use AI tools to work faster and smarter, and you look for ways to automate and augment the finance function rather than throw headcount at it. Excellent judgment, low ego, and high output. You do great work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving environment. Fintech, lead gen/marketing, or financial services experience is a strong plus. Why Juno Work directly with the founders and a high-caliber team on a product with real, measurable impact on people's lives. Own the finance function from the ground up. A culture that values speed, ownership, and using the best modern tools — including AI — to punch above our weight
